play_name: Say the honest thing instead of keeping the peace
behavioral_target: Speaking up honestly instead of going along to avoid tension.
trigger: A hard feeling or a hard topic comes up with someone.
old_play: You stay quiet, act okay, say yes, or say sorry to keep things calm.
function_of_old_play: It avoids a fight and keeps the peace for now.
new_play: Pick one true thing and say it in a calm, kind, and clear way.
what_to_expect: It may feel uncomfortable, and the calm may break for a bit.
why_supports_task: The other person hears the real you, so you can see if you two can work things out — or not.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Saying yes when you mean no; avoiding hard talks; over-apologizing; keeping the peace while unhappy; pretending everything is okay.
context_limitations: These are Cross-Phase behaviors, so the RLC framework has no competencies to ground them. Speaking up should stay calm and kind, not harsh.
review_reason: Cross-Phase: no framework competencies exist to anchor the alternative.

behavioral_target: Naming and asking for a personal need instead of hiding it.
trigger: You have a need in the relationship but feel unsure about voicing it.
old_play: You push the need down or don't bring it up.
function_of_old_play: It keeps things easy and skips a possible no.
new_play: Pick one need. Say it or ask for it in a calm, clear way.
what_to_expect: Asking can feel risky, and they might say no.
why_supports_task: The other person gets a real chance to meet your need, and you see if they do.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Ignoring your own needs; not asking for what you need.
context_limitations: Sources span the Expansion phase and Cross-Phase, so no single competency cleanly maps.
review_reason: Mixed phase; no clean competency for voicing personal needs.

play_name: Do your fair share and let them carry theirs
behavioral_target: Giving at a fair level instead of over-giving or doing it all.
trigger: There is a load of tasks or needs to handle together.
old_play: You give too much or take on everything yourself.
function_of_old_play: It keeps things done and avoids a fight over who does what.
new_play: Do your part, then stop. Leave room for the other person to carry their share.
what_to_expect: Some things may not get done, or not on time or your way.
why_supports_task: You find out if the other person shares the load, or leaves it to you.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Giving too much; always ending up doing everything.
context_limitations: Fits the Expansion task of Integration, where sharing the load is the point.

play_name: Set a limit on staying instead of staying by hope
behavioral_target: Deciding to keep staying only if real change is happening.
trigger: You are in something that may not be working, but leaving feels hard.
old_play: You stay longer than you should.
function_of_old_play: Staying keeps the relationship going for now.
new_play: Pick ahead of time what you need to see, and by when. Then look at what really happened and decide.
what_to_expect: You may face a hard choice or a loss.
why_supports_task: You see if things are truly changing or just hoped for.
context_limitations: This is Context Dependent: staying is fine if things are really getting better, not if it is only hope.
review_reason: Context-dependent; no clean Expansion competency for a self-boundary on staying.
